FAQs

How can I ensure the FastAPI expert understands my project needs?

Start by explaining your project goals and what you want the API to do. Talk about the type of data you’ll handle and how users will interact with it. Clear communication will help the expert use FastAPI to meet your needs accurately.

What qualifications should I look for in a FastAPI freelancer?

Look for someone who has worked with Python and knows FastAPI well. They should have experience with creating APIs and integrating databases. Checking their past projects can help you see if they're the right fit.

How do I define the deliverables for my FastAPI project?

Discuss with the expert the specific outputs you need, like API endpoints and documentation. Make a list of what functions the API should have. This will help ensure both you and the expert are on the same page.

What should I consider when setting deadlines for my FastAPI project?

Think about how complex the API is and any other important dates you have. Talk to the expert about how long the work might take. Realistic deadlines will help ensure quality work without rush.

How can I make sure the FastAPI expert can work with my team?

Ask if they are comfortable using the communication tools your team uses. Discuss any steps they will take to keep you updated on progress. Good communication ensures smooth collaboration.

What are the best ways to track the progress of my FastAPI project?

Use regular check-ins or updates to see how the project is moving along. Ask the expert to share drafts or versions of their work. This helps you provide feedback and ensure the project stays on track.

What should I discuss about maintenance and upgrades with a FastAPI expert?

Talk about how updates to the API should be handled after it's live. Make a plan for dealing with any bugs or improvements needed later. A clear understanding can make future changes smoother.

How do I ensure that the project aligns with my long-term goals?

Discuss with the expert how the current work fits into your future plans. Share anything that might change in the future, like scaling or new features. This foresight helps design an API that grows with you.

Design, Build, AI, Automation
Project Overview Rechitta is a cinematic, feature-film-directed digital web experience engineered for luxury real estate developers in Dubai. It serves as a unified digital briefing engine connecting property developers with over 40,000 registered brokers across 6 international financial hubs at the exact same instant: 04:11 UTC. The landing experience advances through an interconnected five-act sequence: Dawn, the Executive Boardroom, the Broker Terrace, the Synchronised World Chronometer, and the Dusk Horizon Loop. The Problem and Industry Context In rapid-growth luxury property capitals like Dubai, developers launch multi-billion-dollar landmark towers. However, information distribution traditionally relies on outdated and manual workflows: Network Congestion: Over 40,000 registered brokers operating across more than 1,200 independent agencies. The Scheduling Bottleneck: A standard 30-person developer sales team requires 3 to 6 months of repetitive boardroom pitches, phone campaigns, and slide presentations just to brief the local brokerage network. Language Degradation: Cross-border buyers and international brokers speaking Mandarin, Russian, Arabic, Hindi, or French rely on third-party translation relays, causing severe loss of technical nuance, misunderstandings around payment plans, and delayed transaction closings. From an engineering perspective, most scroll-driven video websites attempt to bind scroll offsets directly to the video currentTime property. This introduces decoder starvation, dropped frames, scroll judder, and severe performance issues on mobile devices. Rechitta required an ultra-luxury, fluid 60fps interactive narrative without compromising performance. Key Engineering Architecture and Implementation 1. Discrete Beat Engine and Hardware GPU Decoding To eliminate scroll judder and decoder stalls: Developed a custom input state machine (director.ts) driven by an Intent Accumulator. User scroll wheel and touch gesture events accumulate until crossing a defined threshold before committing to a camera move. Added cooldown guards and idle reset timers to prevent momentum overshoots. Transitions decode short video sequences at native hardware GPU speeds (1.0x to 3.6x) rather than scrub-seeking raw video elements, delivering a locked 60fps playback experience across both desktop and mobile devices. 2. Mathematical 3D Perspective Homography Warp Engine To render live, functioning web applications inside smartphones and boardroom monitors within moving cinematic footage: Built a custom 8-degree-of-freedom perspective homography solver using Gaussian elimination. Tracked normalised video coordinates across corner vertices (Top-Left, Top-Right, Bottom-Right, Bottom-Left) relative to viewport cover crops. Dynamically calculated CSS matrix3d transformations in real time, allowing interactive application interfaces and iframes to naturally track moving physical camera angles. 3. Luminous 3D Orb Navigator and WebGL Globe Built a celestial 3D Orb using Three.js and React Three Fibre that guides the visitor through the narrative. Anchored orb trajectories directly to video clip timestamps rather than scroll percentages, ensuring spatial synchronisation regardless of responsive layout changes. Implemented an interactive 3D WebGL Earth featuring custom atmospheric GLSL Fresnel glow shaders, day/night texture blending, and dynamic marker coordinates for global financial hubs. 4. Synchronised World Chronometer (04:11 UTC) and In-Memory Video Streamer Realised the core philosophy of "The Same Moment" by mathematically calculating simultaneous local times across 6 world capitals (London, Paris, Moscow, Riyadh, Mumbai, Shanghai) from a single 04:11 UTC baseline. Engineered an in-memory RAM Blob pre-warming engine (CityBackdrop.tsx) that precaches high-bitrate drone cinematography loops to ensure instantaneous switching between hubs with native localised typography (supporting both LTR and RTL scripts). 5. Automated Multi-Tier Video Encoding Pipeline Built an automated multi-tier encoding pipeline using FFmpeg to support broad device compatibility: AV1 (10-bit) for modern Chromium browsers. HEVC / Apple VideoToolbox (10-bit) for hardware-accelerated Safari and iOS WebKit rendering. H.264 (8-bit) as a universal baseline fallback. Discretised 60fps WebP keyframes for zero-latency mobile first-frame underlays. 6. Mobile Polish and Continuous Infinity Loop Eliminated video end-of-clip flickering and playback hangs on iOS and Android devices through preloaded dual-video decoders and state cleanups. Designed an architectural infinity loop where the Act V dusk horizon smoothly cross-dissolves backwards into the Act I dawn sky for an uninterrupted, continuous presentation cycle. Design System and Visual Standards Palette: Deep Obsidian (#0A0A09), Surface Obsidian (#141413), Desert Gold (#C5A572), Electric Brand Blue (#3D6FF5), and Warm Off-White (#FAFAF9). Typography: Architectural serif headings paired with clean Swiss grotesque body typography and monospace UTC telemetry clocks. Micro-Interactions: Magnetic custom cursors, glassmorphic HUD status overlays, and fluid layout progress rails. Key Results and Deliverables Consistent 60fps Playback: Fully resolved video judder and decoder starvation across low-power mobile devices and high-end 4K workstations. Cross-Platform Parity: Native hardware video acceleration and responsive touch gestures across iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows. Tested Reliability: Automated unit test coverage powered by Vitest verifying core algorithms including homography matrix calculations, input accumulators, and timeline synchronisation. Luxury Standard: Delivered a high-performance web experience matching the calibre and architectural scale of Dubai's premier property developers. Technology Stack Frontend: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript Styling: Tailwind CSS v4, Vanilla CSS Modules 3D and Animation: Three.js, React Three Fibre, Drei, GSAP, Lenis Smooth Scroll Shaders and Math: Custom GLSL Shaders, 8-DOF Homography Solver (matrix3d) Media Pipeline: FFmpeg (AV1, HEVC, H.264, WebP) Quality Assurance: Vitest, ESLint

Tempies / LevMaps | Social Pet Walking, Discovery & Location App Flutter • Firebase • Shopify • Google Maps • iOS & Android Built a full-featured cross-platform mobile app that brings pet discovery, real-world exploration, social interaction, and commerce into one experience. Tempies / LevMaps lets pet owners discover nearby pets and places, connect with the community, track walks and journeys in real time, and access an integrated shopping experience, all from a single mobile app. I worked across the complete product lifecycle, from application architecture and complex mobile interactions to backend integrations and production deployment across iOS and Android. The app includes real-time GPS tracking and route visualization, interactive maps, user and pet profiles, social feeds, authentication, media and data management, and a Shopify-powered commerce layer. Firebase powers authentication, application services, analytics, performance monitoring, and crash reporting, while the mobile experience is built in Flutter for a consistent native experience across platforms. One of the more technically interesting parts was building the location experience beyond a basic map integration. The app handles live movement tracking, route plotting, distance calculation, journey state, and location permissions, including the additional native considerations required when tracking continues outside the foreground app experience. What we built: Cross-platform iOS + Android app • Real-time GPS & journey tracking • Interactive maps & route visualization • Social/community experience • Pet & user profiles • Authentication • Shopify commerce integration • Firebase backend & services • Crashlytics & performance monitoring • Native mobile permissions & integrations • TestFlight & Google Play deployment Tech stack: Flutter, Firebase, Shopify, Google Maps APIs, native iOS/Android integrations From product UI to real-time location infrastructure to App Store deployment, this was a proper end-to-end mobile build rather than a dressed-up web app in a mobile shell. Built for the real world. Literally. http://levmaps.com./

Peoplecite.tech (https://Peoplecite.tech) finds you the people you need for your business needs. The problem Recruiters, investors, event organizers and journalists all have to find specific people. Their tools haven't kept up. People databases go stale, keyword search returns hundreds of weak matches, and the manual route takes hours of searching, opening tabs and cross-checking. When a tool does produce a list, it rarely explains why a name made the cut, so you can't trust it without checking every entry again. The idea Describe the people you need the way you'd brief a colleague. PeopleCite researches the live web and returns a slate: a ranked list where every name comes with receipts. "Staff payments engineers with Series B–C experience" → a ranked shortlist with evidence, not 400 keyword hits "Technical founders building in industrial automation" → people who aren't on anyone's list yet "Climate scientists who can hold a stage" → speakers with their press footprint attached How it works for the user Ask in plain language. There are no boolean strings or filters. You give the role, field, constraints and dealbreakers. Watch the research happen. Several researchers work through the brief in parallel. The user sees each step live: what's being searched, what's being read, and who's being considered. A typical run takes 5–20 minutes, and closing the tab doesn't stop it. Review a slate with receipts. Each person arrives with: a fit score against your criteria a written rationale a verification status (verified, likely or flagged) links to every source used One click exports the slate to Excel or CSV. Beyond a single search Monitors: saved searches re-run on a schedule, and a digest email lists only the new people. CSV enrichment: upload your own list and get back verified evidence for each person. Outreach drafts: a first message for any candidate, written from the research. Exclusion lists: people you've already seen or contacted stay out of future results. Team workspaces: shared seats and shared runs for agencies and teams. API + MCP: PeopleCite works inside other tools and AI assistants, such as Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor. Design decisions that mattered Trust over volume. The product is built around receipts. If something can't be verified, such as a person's location, it is flagged rather than guessed. Results are presented as research leads, not hiring decisions, and the user always reviews and decides. Long-running work that feels instant. A deep research run can take many minutes. The interface streams progress as it happens, so the wait feels like watching work get done. Runs continue on their own if the user leaves. Pricing that matches value. Users pay per candidate researched, not per seat. Credits scale with research depth (Fast, Smart, Deep), so a 10-person search has a predictable cost. There are three tiers ($49 / $149 / $399 a month) and a 14-day free trial. Responsible by default. The product has no demographic targeting of any kind. Users can export or delete their data at any time, and every claim traces back to a source. It ships with a privacy policy and a DPA. Outcome PeopleCite went from first commit to a public, paid product on its own domain in about three months. At launch it had subscription billing, a free trial, team seats, scheduled monitors, an API and an MCP server. The landing page uses no stock imagery. Its hero section replays a real research run.

Crawrix.ai (https://Crawrix.ai) - AI Agent that does SEO, GEO and AEO for you. Find out what AI says about your business, then fix it. More people now ask an AI assistant for a recommendation instead of searching Google. Most small businesses don't know if they appear in those answers. The crawlers behind them don't run JavaScript, so plenty of sites are invisible to them and nobody notices. Crawrix measures this. It asks AI models about the business and its category, runs search-grounded checks through Perplexity, and crawls the site for what answer engines read: AI-crawler access in robots.txt, llms.txt, structured data, sitemaps, and pages that answer real customer questions. The output is one score with a history, so an owner can see whether a change helped. A chat agent then works through the fixes. With a GitHub repo connected, it reads the codebase, writes the change and opens a pull request. It knows Next.js, Astro and other frameworks, and it can audit a live URL when there's no repo at all. Every write stops at an approval card that shows the diff first. Key features AI visibility score built from three parts: what models already know about the business, how it shows up in AI search, and how ready the site is for AI crawlers Ranked fix plan, with step-by-step guided cards for changes made by hand Chat agent that audits code and live pages, including Lighthouse runs in a sandboxed browser Pull requests generated from findings, each gated behind owner approval One agent, three ways to use it: the web app, a command-line tool (TypeScript and Rust builds), and an MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor and other MCP clients Scheduled re-scans that keep the score history current Connections to your own MCP servers, with OAuth and encrypted credential storage WordPress, Wix, Webflow and Framer integrations in progress, so sites without a repo get the same approve-then-apply flow
